notes: No P16 solver or MUMPS candidate was adopted. Final solver binaries must match the P15 baseline.
The benchmark retains probe history, configurable original-margin (default 0.5), and interleaved initial-block filters.
All measured screens use the unchanged 0.5 residual acceptance margin and 1e-10 original tolerance.

The first width screen used the pre-enhancement P15 block benchmark with fixed 0.5 margin. Its source is saved but its ELF was not separately copied before rebuilding. Later screens use the separately saved bench-block, bench-start and bench-purified executables.
The block benchmark omits exact certificates. It is a same-factorization screen, not an end-to-end or open-source comparison.
Initial filter construction time and extra shift-invert applications are included explicitly in the benchmark results.
Panel scalar arithmetic uses separate multiply/subtract without FMA contraction. PIVSIZ=2 delegates to original MUMPS.

Panel probes compare all output buffer bytes, including padding, and output metadata, for finite rational inputs with PIVSIZ=1. They are not a proof for arbitrary floating-point inputs or every MUMPS path.
Panel width 0 microbenchmark forwards through the interposer; full-solve baseline does not preload it.
Seven repetitions per case per panel variant, all 98 solves independently evaluated; timing geomean is essentially unchanged.
The halfslab memset trace is diagnostic with interception overhead and was not independently evaluated.
The archive contains logs, source prototypes, patches and all evaluation JSON, but excludes binaries and eigenvector NPY files. Those remain in the remote experiment directory.
No claim that all open-source implementations or all workloads have been beaten.
